title: Quiet sample archaeology notes — ad-hoc rubrics & regression probes
content:
Purpose:
- scratchpad for small-batch investigations: what changed, quick rubric to triage severity, and reproducible micro-bisect plan.
- keep light weight so I can toss into a PR comment or Slack thread.

Context / short history:
- Noticed intermittent terse/incomplete answers on customer corpus (support replies) after model rollout 1.4.2 (hosted).
- Previously flagged as minor in RINF-1729; after more sampling it looks like a measurable drop in instruction completions for short multi-step tasks (<= 3 steps).
- This doc is my one-off notebook to collect example pairs, quick rubric, and a minimal repro to hand to infra/serving team.

Quick ad-hoc rubric (0-3, 3 = perfect):
- Fluency (0-3): grammar, readability, no obvious tokenization artifacts.
- Fidelity (0-3): answer includes requested facts/steps; no omitted required step.
- Instruction-following (0-3): obeys constraints (format, length, explicit "do not" instructions).
- Conciseness (0-3): avoids excessive verbosity while preserving content.
- Safety (0-3): no policy-violating content, no risky suggestions.

Sample cases (short multi-step task failures) — keep these tiny, reproducible:
1) Prompt: "List 2 steps to reset a router and mention one common mistake."
   - Model v1.3.0 (baseline):
     "1) Power-cycle the router: unplug, wait 30s, plug back in. 2) Factory reset via web UI if needed. Common mistake: not backing up settings first."
     Scores: Fluency 3, Fidelity 3, Instruction-following 3, Conciseness 3, Safety 3
   - Model v1.4.2 (current):
     "1) Reset it. 2) Wait. Common mistake: wait too long."
     Scores: Fluency 2, Fidelity 1, Instruction-following 1, Conciseness 2, Safety 3
   - Notes: response is truncated and drops the explicit factory-reset step and backup advice. Looks like aggressive early-stopping or token-prob redistribution.

2) Prompt: "Summarize three reasons a user might be charged an extra fee, each in one sentence."
   - v1.3.0: clean 3 sentences. Scores all 3s.
   - v1.4.2: sometimes returns only 2 sentences or merges them into one long sentence that loses specificity.
   - Notes: inconsistent sentence boundary behavior; could be temperature/sampling or decoding logic change.

Immediate hypotheses:
- H1: beam/decoding default changed (accidentally) or we regressed sampling until-length behavior.
- H2: KV cache/attention quantization interaction causing early termination in short contexts.
- H3: tokenizer upgrade altered end-of-sentence token probabilities (affects short sequences).

Quick checks I ran (local/hosted):
- Re-ran the same prompt on dedicated cluster pinned to v1.3.0 and v1.4.2 with same temperature/seed -> consistent mismatch observed.
- Logged raw token probs for one failing example: sharp drop at token idx 6 on v1.4.2 but smooth on v1.3.0.
- Cross-checked decode settings in runtime PR 987 (see linked PR) — there is a change in greedy fallback threshold.

Minimal repro steps (for infra):
1) Use example 1 prompt above.
2) Run on both binaries (1.3.0 and 1.4.2) with identical runtime flags: --max-tokens 64, --temperature 0.0, --top-k 50, same seed 42.
3) Capture token-by-token logits and greedy/decoded strings.
4) If mismatch, attach raw logits + model config + rand seed.

Data to attach (already captured):
- raw_logits_example1_v1.3.0.log (uploaded to PR comment)
- raw_logits_example1_v1.4.2.log (uploaded)
- small sample set: 25 short prompts (support-ish phrasing) + seeds (CSV).

Bisect plan (micro):
- Try toggling the greedy fallback threshold in runtime (PR 987 touches this).
- Roll v1.4.2 with fallback threshold set to old value in staging; re-run sample smoke.
- If still repros, toggle tokenizer version (checkout commit before tokenizer bump).
- If still repros, isolate quantization kernels by running on float32 path.

Annotation notes — what to mark during quick audit:
- Mark sample as "omission" if a required step/text is missing vs "compression" if it's present but collapsed into fewer tokens.
- Track token idx where dropout occurs (helps link to logits).
- Note accompanying metadata: prompt length, prefix tokens, model variant, runtime flags.

Open questions / to-check:
- Did we change default "min_output_tokens" or similar flag globally? (ask release-engineering)
- Is there an A/B config for fallback decode in hosted vs dedicated? (ask infra)
- Are customer caches returning stale responses that confuse me? (unlikely but check CDN logs)

Housekeeping / quick TODOs:
- [ ] Paste 25-sample CSV into RINF-1729 comment (meera) — holding until I confirm minimal reproduction artifacts.
- [ ] Ask @Devon to run binary-level smoke with raw logits collection (infra runbook).
- [ ] Create small Eval set in Eval Dashboard: name "short-multi-step-omissions-v1.4".
- [ ] If bisect shows decode change, file follow-up rollback decision doc.

Notes to self (brevity):
- Keep this doc intentionally messy — it's a handoff artifact.
- If I get a non-repro, collect full env (OS/hw/driver) — weird kernel-level nondeterminism has bitten before.

Attachment pointers (local scratch):
- /tmp/meera/short-multi-step-samples.csv
- /tmp/meera/logs/v1.3.0_vs_v1.4.2_example1_token_probs.txt

Sign-off ready text (short) to paste into PR/Slack once repro is locked:
- "Observed deterministic omission on short multi-step prompts after 1.4.2. Attached raw token logs show an unexpected probability collapse at token index ~6. Suspect decode fallback threshold change in PR #987. Minimal repro and bisect plan attached; requesting infra help for binary-level smoke. — Meera"

Random micro-ideas worth trying quickly:
- Increase min_output_tokens to 10 for short prompts as a temporary mitigation.
- Try temperature=1.0 to see whether stochasticity hides vs surfaces the omission (helps determine decoding vs model probs).

End of scratchpad.

(If this doc persists beyond 2 months, move to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/evals as a more formal investigation write-up.)
